published.name: Bella Vista Farm Park
published.description: Set on a prominent hilltop across 20 hectares of rural landscape at Elizabeth Macarthur Drive, this is an intact historic farm complex established in the late 1700s. A two-storey homestead, a Bunya Pine lined driveway and various farm outbuildings survive as a link to some of Australia's earliest rural development and its first European settlers. The property passed into the ownership of The Hills Shire Council in 1998, which has adopted a Conservation Management Plan guiding its restoration. The surrounding grounds are open to the public, with walking tracks, and dogs are welcome on-leash.

published.name: Museum of Printing
published.description:
A working letterpress museum on the Penrith Paceway grounds, west of Sydney, opposite the stadium being built for the Penrith Panthers. Volunteers keep the machinery running: hand-set type cases, Ludlow, Linotype, wooden type, a Vandercook press and a 1936 Heidelberg Cylinder press. Visitors can try hand typesetting as Gutenberg did in the 1400s and print on presses from the mid-1800s. Rare books and newspapers are on display, including a facsimile of the Gutenberg Bible.

The museum runs day-long letterpress workshops in typography, poster and Adana printing, and hosts Rare Book Week talks and demonstrations. Open to the public on Sundays or by appointment.

published.name: Twisted Science
published.description:
A hands-on science centre in the old Holmesglen TAFE campus on Bulli Street, run by founder Kathy Stubberfield, who began the venture as The Scientwists and opened her first centre in her hometown of Echuca. Everything here is taken out of the box to be touched, moved, built and played with, and a no-instructions policy keeps reading to a minimum. The exhibit floor splits into three areas: blue and green for all ages, and tangerine, a private space for pre-schoolers with a cocooned area for under-twos. Natural sunlight is used throughout rather than dark accent lighting.

The Snack Lab Cafe pours locally roasted Arabica coffee and science drinks served in beakers and conical flasks, and the gift shop stocks science toys, puzzles and edible bugs.
published.meritSplit: chain: TwistED Science operates multiple science centres (Moorabbin and Echuca) and describes itself as a company that builds and runs centres, making it a small chain rather than a single independent place.

published.name: The Reef Retreat
published.description: Boutique accommodation spread across three separate properties in Palm Cove, all a short walk from the beach and Esplanade. The main retreat at 10–14 Harpa Street sits within a Melaleuca rainforest setting of tropical gardens, native plants and birdlife, with self-contained studios, suites and apartments sharing a heated pool and spa and a BBQ and entertainment area. Four three-bedroom townhouses stand opposite on Harpa Street, and the Tranquility Apartments sit a block away on Amphora Street. One of the original accommodation properties in the village, it runs an onsite tour desk to help guests arrange trips through Tropical North Queensland.
published.meritSplit: local: Generic self-contained holiday apartment complex near the beach with no distinctive design, history, or identity beyond a standard boutique-branded rental operation.

published.name: Balmoral Hotel
published.description: A pub on Albany Highway in East Victoria Park, within a short drive of McCallum Park and the Swan River. The Bistro serves modern takes on pub classics — steaks, seafood, salads and shared platters — made with ingredients from local suppliers, with a focus on food meant to be shared. There are three bars stocking local and imported beer, wine, cider and spirits, and a beer garden with a large screen for watching sport and space for live music. Six function spaces cater to events of varying sizes.
published.meritSplit: local: Generic pub with bistro, bars and function rooms; nothing distinctive it makes, brews or shows that would warrant going out of your way.

published.name: Brisbane Tramway Museum
published.description: Founded in 1968 and opened to the public in 1980, this volunteer-run museum preserves Brisbane's tramway history in a bushland setting at Ferny Grove, next to the Bowls Club. Six working trams dating from 1901 to 1962 carry visitors on rides each Sunday afternoon, weather permitting. Alongside the trams are depot stations, a signal cabin, historical photographs and a gift shop of tramway memorabilia. A Men's Shed operates within the grounds, meeting on Tuesdays. The museum runs as a not-for-profit and takes group bookings for schools, clubs and occasions.

published.name: The Australian Armour & Artillery Museum
published.description: A privately owned collection in Smithfield, north of Cairns, dedicated to the collection, preservation, restoration and display of armoured vehicles and artillery from the 1800s to the present day, with a particular focus on WWII. It holds over 240 vehicles and artillery pieces, drawn from both world wars, many not found elsewhere in Australia. The museum opened to the public on 6 September 2014. Visitors can take armoured vehicle rides and, under the supervision of qualified safety officers, fire military bolt action rifles in the shooting gallery.

published.name: Home on Darley
published.description: A homewares and interiors shop at 3 Bungan Street, Mona Vale. The stock runs to French linen bedding and loungewear, quilts, sheets and pillows, jute and wool rugs, cushions, throws, brass homewares and bathroom accessories, along with soaps, candles and doormats. Kitchen and dining pieces include glassware, napkins, placemats and coasters. Staffed daily, with shorter hours on Sunday.
published.meritSplit: local: A generic homewares reseller stocking mass-market bedding and décor brands, with no distinctive making, curation or identity of its own.
